modules.title: Introduction to Electromagnetism
modules.content:
The Four Fundamental Forces

Every force in nature belongs to one of these four categories:

  • Gravitational Force: Weakest force, acts between any two bodies due to mass.
  • Electromagnetic Force: Responsible for attraction/repulsion of charges and magnetic effects.
  • Strong Nuclear Force: Holds protons and neutrons together in atomic nucleus.
  • Weak Nuclear Force: Responsible for Beta decay.
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain the difference between the four fundamental forces to a 10-year-old using a simple analogy.

flashcards.definition: The force responsible for attraction/repulsion of electric charges and magnetic effects.
The force that holds protons and neutrons together in the atomic nucleus.

micro_quiz.question: Which fundamental force is responsible for keeping electrons bound to the atomic nucleus?
micro_quiz.explanation: The electromagnetic force causes the attraction between the positively charged protons in the nucleus and the negatively charged electrons.

modules.title: Electric Charge & Its Properties
modules.content:
What is Electric Charge?

Electric charge is a fundamental physical quantity of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electric field.

Key Properties:

  1. Quantization: Charge exists in discrete units. q = ne (where n = 0, ±1, ±2...)
  2. Conservation: Total charge in an isolated system remains constant.
  3. Attraction & Repulsion: Like charges repel, unlike charges attract.
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain why charge is 'quantized' using a simple real-world analogy.

flashcards.definition: The smallest unit of electric charge: e ≈ 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ Coulombs.
The total electric charge in an isolated system remains constant over time.

micro_quiz.question: If you remove 1000 electrons from a neutral object, what is its net charge?
micro_quiz.explanation: Removing electrons (negative charge) leaves a positive charge. Q = 1000 × (+1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C) = +1.602×10¹⁶ C
